hypotheses.name: fill_drain
hypotheses.prediction: Fixed extra cost is amortized for longer K; long-stage slope should not worsen if this is the only cause.
hypotheses.intervention: Sweep stages at fixed tile, compiler path and timing boundary; fit intercept and slope.

hypotheses.name: residency
hypotheses.prediction: Single CTA can improve while the grid gets slower near a resource threshold.
hypotheses.intervention: Record actual allocated resources and active CTAs; compare one CTA with many, and vary an isolated capacity budget.

hypotheses.name: spill
hypotheses.prediction: Additional local-memory traffic persists per stage and may worsen the long-stage slope.
hypotheses.intervention: Inspect generated program/local traffic; shorten unrelated live ranges while recording all changed resources.

hypotheses.name: unrealized_overlap
hypotheses.prediction: Async source expressions do not shorten actual exposed copy/compute gaps.
hypotheses.intervention: Inspect generated instructions and hardware timelines with the same logical work.

hypotheses.name: preparation_or_contention
hypotheses.prediction: Full-call cost or multi-CTA copy/compute rates differ despite the single-CTA model.
hypotheses.intervention: Separate preparation from kernel and measure L/I/C as a function of residency.

scope: Cross-agent reading and independent changed-shape CPU exercise with inherited parent context; no OS isolation, fixed budget, GPU execution or controlled knowledge-gain estimate.
limits: Python scalar operations do not prove FP32 SIMT rounding or compiled instruction correctness.
The declared event recurrence and nonoverlapping wave model are synthetic assumptions, not measured GPU behavior.
